denyNamespaces.description: Namespaces the plugin's actions refuse, whatever the role. A JSON list in the environment.

auth.description: How dash authenticates to Alertmanager. Neither basic nor bearerToken sends no credentials.

enabled.description: false turns the plugin off: its topics are removed, and the web UI drops its rail entry, palette entries, overview tiles and panels and shows a switched-off page at its address. Unset turns it on when it has the settings it needs; a plugin without them is disabled ("not configured: set plugins.<id>.url", naming the setting to make) and the web UI hides its pages. true with settings missing or invalid makes it unconfigured, which hides its pages too. This is how prometheus, alertmanager, gatus, victorialogs, proxmox, hardware, kubernetes, grafana, headlamp and launcher behave, and a change to any of their settings applies live: that plugin restarts, and so do the plugins that use or require it (a prometheus change restarts proxmox, hardware and kubernetes; a gatus change restarts hardware and kubernetes; a proxmox change restarts hardware; a kubernetes change restarts proxmox; a grafana change restarts alertmanager). flux has not moved to a plugin of its own yet: a change to it needs a restart.

ignoreAlerts.description: Alert names dash drops everywhere: the alert list, the attention items and the firing count. A JSON list in the environment.

protectedAlerts.description: Alert names nobody can silence through dash, whatever the role. A JSON list in the environment.

severityMap.description: How an alert's severity label value becomes dash's severity (crit or warn), as {label value: severity}. A JSON object in the environment.

silenceDurations.description: The silence lengths the dialog offers, from 1h, 4h, 24h and 7d. A JSON list in the environment.

basic.description: HTTP Basic authentication. Not together with bearerToken.

label.description: The row's name. Empty names each row after its CronJob.

tags.description: VM tags that make a VM critical (compared without regard to case). A JSON list in the environment.

hosts.description: The machine behind the cluster, as [{name, nodename, model, bays, fanMaxRPM, sensorAliases}]; every key is optional, and [{}] reads the Proxmox node, which needs the proxmox plugin to run (its URL, token ID and token secret set) unless nodename is set. One entry is supported for now. A JSON list in the environment.

machines.description: Machines outside the cluster to show as up or down, as [{name, nodeExporterNodename}] (up while their node-exporter is scraped) or [{name, gatusEndpoint}] (up while that Gatus check passes). A JSON list in the environment.

selectors.description: The label values dash's queries select by.

tempThresholds.description: CPU package temperature, in °C, at which the host turns warning and critical (whole degrees).

type.description: The plugin type. dash runs one instance per type, so this is empty or the section name.

zfsScrubMetricPrefix.description: Prefix of the ZFS scrub series: <prefix>_last_end_timestamp_seconds, <prefix>_last_errors and <prefix>_in_progress. Must be a valid metric name. Empty queries no scrub data and the pool cards show none.

bays.description: Drive bays the Disks grid draws, 0 to 128. 0 numbers the slots from 1 (from 0 when a disk sits in slot 0) up to the highest one that holds a disk, at most 128; above that, or when the disks' bay labels are not distinct numbers, the page lists the disks sorted.

fanMaxRPM.description: Top of the fan gauges, in RPM, 0 to 100000. 0 scales them to the fastest fan seen. A gauge never ends below the speed a fan reports.

model.description: Shown next to the host's name, e.g. Dell R730.

name.description: The host's name in the web UI. Empty uses the Proxmox node's name, then the nodename.

nodename.description: The nodename label of the host's node-exporter and IPMI series. Empty uses the node of the running proxmox plugin (plugins.proxmox.node, or the node it discovers), so the plugin needs its URL, token ID and token secret; without it the Hardware row stays unavailable (waiting for the Proxmox node name) until nodename is set.

sensorAliases.description: Which temperature sensors the Inlet and Exhaust tiles read.

gatusEndpoint.description: The name of the Gatus check that tells whether the machine is reachable (compared without regard to case). A check that does not exist counts as down. Exactly one of nodeExporterNodename and gatusEndpoint.

name.description: The machine's name in the web UI, unique ignoring case, at most 64 bytes.

nodeExporterNodename.description: The nodename label of the machine's node-exporter: it is up while the node-exporter is scraped. Exactly one of nodeExporterNodename and gatusEndpoint.

hwmonChip.description: RE2 regular expression for the chip label of the CPU package temperature (node_hwmon_temp_celsius), e.g. platform_coretemp_.* for Intel.

nodeExporterJob.description: The job label of the node-exporter targets, which the machines' up queries select.

exhaust.description: Text the exhaust sensor's name contains, ignoring case. Empty means exhaust.

inlet.description: Text the inlet sensor's name contains, ignoring case. Empty means inlet.

cluster.description: Name of the cluster in Headlamp's URLs.

type.description: The plugin type. dash runs one instance per type, so this is empty or the section name.

url.description: Base URL of Headlamp, e.g. https://headlamp.example.com. Empty turns the deep links off.

backupJobs.description: The CronJobs behind the backup ages, as [{namespace, cronjob, label}] (up to 8). cronjob also matches every CronJob named cronjob-<suffix>. label names the row; empty names each row after the CronJob. Empty hides the backup rows. A JSON list in the environment.

burst.description: Burst of requests the client may send at once, at least qps. The default is 40.

context.description: The kubeconfig context to use. Empty uses the kubeconfig's current context. Only read with a kubeconfig.

conventions.description: Labels dash reads from namespaces. None has a default: while one is empty the feature that depends on it is off.

kubeconfig.description: Path of a kubeconfig file, used outside the cluster (development). Empty means the in-cluster configuration. The standard KUBECONFIG variable fills it too; this setting's own variable wins.

mode.description: How dash reaches the cluster: auto uses the kubeconfig when kubeconfig (or the standard KUBECONFIG variable) is set, else the in-cluster configuration, else runs without a cluster (the plugin is unavailable and the pages that need it are hidden); inCluster and kubeconfig insist on that one source and report an error when it is missing.

optional.description: CRDs that a cluster may not have. A missing CRD of the kinds the plugin reads shows as a note and makes the plugin degraded, unless it is marked optional here.

qps.description: Requests per second dash's Kubernetes client may send, above 0. The default is 20.

type.description: The plugin type. dash runs one instance per type, so this is empty or the section name.

upstreamViaAPIServer.description: Send the requests of the other plugins to in-cluster service URLs (http://<service>.<namespace>.svc) through the API server's service proxy, with the Kubernetes credentials. For running dash on a laptop against a remote cluster (development); off by default. Applies to requests made after the plugin starts.

appsFluxPrefix.description: Namespaces applied by a Flux Kustomization whose name starts with this prefix are listed under Apps. Empty turns the grouping off.

protectedLabel.description: Namespace label (value "true") that makes a restart ask you to type the namespace name. Empty protects no namespace.

tenantLabel.description: Namespace label that puts the namespace under Tenants; its value is the tenant. Empty turns the grouping off.

job.description: The job label of etcd's metrics in Prometheus. The default is etcd.

certificates.description: The cluster may lack the cert-manager CRDs: their absence is not a note.

externalSecrets.description: The cluster may lack the external-secrets CRDs: their absence is not a note.

httpRoutes.description: The cluster may lack the Gateway API CRDs: their absence is not a note.

file.description: Path of a YAML or JSON file with the launcher's links (see docs/launcher.example.yaml). The file is read when the launcher starts: restart dash, or change the launcher's settings, to read it again; an unreadable file makes the launcher report an error. Not together with links.

links.description: The launcher's links, inline: a list of {name, href, icon, description}. icon is an icon name (resolved against ui.iconBaseURL; without it the link shows a letter tile), a same-origin path, or an image URL under ui.iconBaseURL. Not together with file.

type.description: The plugin type. dash runs one instance per type, so this is empty or the section name.

bodyReadTimeout.description: A request body must arrive within this long.

maxHeaderBytes.description: Largest request header block the API listener accepts, in bytes.

sseWriteTimeout.description: A stalled stream write fails after this long.

streams.description: Open /api/v1/stream connections in all; more get 503.

streamsPerUser.description: Open /api/v1/stream connections one user may hold; more get 429.

tailMaxDuration.description: A log tail ends after this long and the browser reconnects.

tails.description: Open plugin stream connections (the log tail) in all; more get 503.

tailsPerUser.description: Open plugin stream connections (the log tail) one user may hold; more get 429.

flux.description: Flux: how dash reads Flux objects.

hardware.description: The physical host behind the cluster.

headlamp.description: Headlamp: deep links into the Kubernetes UI.

kubernetes.description: Kubernetes: how dash reaches and reads the cluster.

launcher.description: The launcher: links to your infrastructure.

proxmox.description: Proxmox VE: virtual machines, containers and the hypervisor.

victorialogs.description: VictoriaLogs: the pod logs the UI shows.

headers.description: Extra headers sent with every request, as {name: value}. Plain configuration, not secrets: put credentials in auth. Authorization, Proxy-Authorization, Cookie and Host cannot be set. A JSON object in the environment.

timeout.description: How long one query may take before dash gives up on it.

tls.description: How dash verifies the service's certificate.

criticalVMs.description: Which VMs are critical. No VM is critical by default.

node.description: The Proxmox node to read. Empty is discovered from the API when the cluster has exactly one node; set it for several nodes or to skip discovery. The hardware plugin reads the host's node from the running proxmox plugin, so without hosts[0].nodename it needs Proxmox to run (url, tokenID and tokenSecret all set).

series.description: How the VM chart queries select a VM.

storage.description: Where the Proxmox storage list comes from.

tls.description: How dash verifies the Proxmox API's certificate.

tokenID.description: API token ID, user@realm!tokenname. Proxmox runs only with url, tokenID and tokenSecret all set and is disabled with none of the token set. A token ID without tokenSecret, a tokenSecret without tokenID, or a token without url is a configuration error that stops dash at startup.

tokenSecret.description: API token secret: a literal, env:NAME or file:/path. Set together with tokenID: one without the other is a configuration error.

type.description: The plugin type. dash runs one instance per type, so this is empty or the section name.

url.description: Base URL of the Proxmox API, e.g. https://pve.example.com:8006. Required with a token; a URL alone leaves Proxmox disabled.

vmSelector.description: The label matcher that selects one VM in the pve-exporter series of the VM charts: one label, = or =~, and a quoted value with {vmid} once, e.g. id="qemu/{vmid}".

source.description: Where the storage list comes from: api reads the node's storages from the Proxmox API (the API token needs the Datastore.Audit privilege on /storage); prometheus reads the pve-exporter series pve_disk_usage_bytes, pve_disk_size_bytes and pve_storage_info through the prometheus plugin.

allowedHosts.description: Host names the API answers besides the host of publicURL: names or IP addresses without scheme or port. ["*"] accepts any. A JSON list in the environment.

healthListen.description: Address of /healthz and /readyz. In dev and demo mode it defaults to 127.0.0.1:8081.

limits.description: What one client, and all clients together, may hold open or send.

listen.description: Address of the API and the web UI, reached through the identity proxy. Dev mode only accepts a loopback address.

metrics.description: Serve dash's own Prometheus metrics at /metrics on the health listener. Off by default. The listener is unauthenticated and the metrics name plugins and their states, so keep it cluster-internal.

publicURL.description: The URL people open, with scheme and host (https://dash.example.com). Required; the only Origin accepted on writes. In dev and demo mode it defaults to http://localhost:5173.

readyRequires.description: Plugins /readyz waits for: each listed plugin must have finished starting (its first poll or cache sync) before dash reports ready, up to readyTimeout. Empty: /readyz needs only that dash is serving and every plugin's start has returned. Names are plugins.<id> sections, e.g. ["kubernetes"]. A JSON list in the environment.

readyTimeout.description: How long /readyz waits for the readyRequires plugins, counted from startup. After that dash reports ready anyway and logs a warning naming the plugins still starting.

ui.description: Whether the settings page may save values: editable, or readonly (fully managed, GitOps). A data directory that is missing or not writable is read-only either way.

caFile.description: Path of a PEM file with the certificate authority that signed the service's certificate, added to the system roots. Empty uses the system roots only.

insecureSkipVerify.description: Skip verifying the service's certificate and host name. Anyone on the network path can then impersonate the service: prefer caFile.

crit.description: The CPU package temperature, in °C, from which the host is critical.

warn.description: The CPU package temperature, in °C, from which the host is warning. Greater than zero and below crit.

iconBaseURL.description: Where the icons of launcher links resolve: a launcher icon called proxmox is requested from <iconBaseURL>/proxmox.png, and an absolute icon URL on a launcher link is used only when it lies under this URL. App icons on the Apps page are not affected in this release: they still come from the server-built CDN URL until a later release. An http(s) URL with a host, without query or fragment, e.g. https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/homarr-labs/dashboard-icons/png. Empty (the default) shows letter tiles for launcher links, so the launcher makes no third-party request.

auth.description: How dash authenticates to VictoriaLogs. Neither basic nor bearerToken sends no credentials.

denyNamespaces.description: Namespaces whose logs dash refuses to show, whatever the role. A JSON list in the environment.

fields.description: The field names of the log records that identify the pod. Letters, digits, underscores and dots, not starting with a digit or a dot.

limit.description: Most log lines one query returns. Greater than zero.

type.description: The plugin type. dash runs one instance per type, so this is empty or the section name.

url.description: Base URL of the service, e.g. http://host:9090. Empty turns the source off: dash makes no request and its panels show "source not configured".

description: The dash config file. The environment overrides it, setting by setting: DASH_ plus the path in UPPER_SNAKE case.

dataDir.description: Where dash keeps its state (ui-settings.yaml, audit.jsonl) and looks for config.yaml. Demo mode uses none.

plugins.description: One section per plugin. An empty URL turns that source off.

server.description: How dash listens and what it calls itself.

settings.description: The settings store behind the settings page.

ui.description: What the web UI is told by the server.
